verdict.rationale: Maritime has its own sleep/wake lifecycle: agents and web apps go to sleep when idle and wake on the next message or visit. The agent's disk persists while it sleeps and can be browsed through the Files API, so filesystem state survives a sleep. Nothing shows that memory or process state is preserved across sleep, and sleep is idle-triggered rather than a documented developer-initiated pause. Missing for 10: an explicit pause/resume API or command, preservation of memory/process state across sleep, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can pause a running sandbox and resume it later with filesystem and memory state intact

citations.quote: three endpoints get you sleep/wake, channels, and triggers
puts it to sleep when idle, and wakes it on the next visit
browse, upload, download, and edit an agent's disk over HTTP, even while the agent sleeps
